newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK bourse says members reject longer trade hours.
newsitem.headline: HK bourse says members reject longer trade hours.

text.p: The Hong Kong stock exchange said on Thursday a majority of its members had rejected a suggestion that trading hours should be extended.
The exchange floated the idea of a pre-opening session and a later market close in a consultation paper issued in January.
"The finding of the consultation is that the majority says no...The majority says it is not necessary at this stage," a stock exchange spokesman told Reuters.
Hong Kong's trading hours now consist of a morning session from 10.00 a.m. (0200 GMT) to 12.30 p.m. (0430 GMT) and an afternoon session from 2.30 p.m. (0630 GMT) to 3.55 p.m. (0755 GMT).
The spokesman said the findings of the consultation suggested members were not losing business to London and therefore an extension of trading hours was not justified.
Hong Kong shares can be traded in London from 4.30 p.m. (0830 GMT).
The spokesman said the findings would be submitted to the exchange's council at its next meeting.
